expectations.text: Every extracted item includes a rationale explaining why it was extracted
expectations.evidence: All 10 items include a 'Rationale for extraction' field with substantive explanations. Examples: Item 1 explains implications for VQ-VAE probing experiments; Item 3 explains how it nuances existing understanding of the performance gap; Item 8 explains how Levenshtein adds a pairwise comparison dimension to the existing analysis toolkit.

expectations.text: Extracted titles are phrased as claims/propositions, not topic labels
expectations.evidence: Checking 3 representative proposed titles: (1) 'caller identity is encoded more strongly than call-type in discrete acoustic tokens from animal vocalizations' — propositional claim. (2) 'Levenshtein plus k-NN classification loses information that VQ token sequences demonstrably contain' — propositional claim. (3) 'simpler discretization methods tend to outperform theoretically superior ones in bioacoustic representation learning' — propositional claim. All pass the composability test ('This note argues that [title]').

expectations.text: At least 3 distinct categories are represented (e.g. core claims, implementation ideas, tensions)
expectations.evidence: 5 distinct categories represented: Finding (items 1,2,7), Tension (items 3,9), Method (items 4,5), Open question (items 6,10), Implementation idea (item 8). Summary Statistics table confirms all 5 categories.

expectations.text: Report mentions checking existing notes for duplicates or overlap
expectations.evidence: Lines 10-23: Detailed 'Duplicate/Overlap Assessment' section listing 6 existing vault notes with coverage descriptions. expectations.text: The codebook collapse finding (GVQ underperforms VQ due to collapse) is captured as an extraction
expectations.evidence: The GVQ codebook collapse finding is NOT extracted as a standalone item. It is mentioned in the Duplicate/Overlap Assessment (line 18) as already covered by existing note 'Gumbel-softmax VQ suffered severe codebook collapse in bioacoustic token experiments'. Item 9 discusses the broader pattern that 'simpler discretization methods tend to outperform theoretically superior ones' which references GVQ collapse, but this is a generalization/pattern rather than a direct capture of the collapse finding itself. The report explicitly skipped this as already in the vault.
